senses.gloss: (b. h. root in מִשְׁרָה)to dissolve, soak, steep.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Nazir 6:1">Naz. VI, 1</cite> <he>ש׳ פתו ביין וכ׳</he> if he (the Nazirite) steeped his bread in wine, and there is enough in both together to make up the size of an olive; <cite ref="Pesachim 44b:1">Pes. 44ᵇ</cite>.
<cite ref="Nazir 37a:6">Naz. 37ᵃ</cite> <he>אם ש׳ ענביו במים וכ׳</he> if he steeped grapes in water, and a taste of wine remained in it.

<cite ref="Mishnah Pesachim 2:7">Pes. II, 7</cite> <he>אין שׁוֹרִין וכ׳</he> you dare not soak bran for chickens (on the Passover); <cite ref="Mishnah Pesachim 2:7">ib.</cite> <he>האשה לא תִשְׁרֶה וכ׳</he> a woman must not soak bran to take with her to the bathhouse.

<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 1:5">Sabb. I, 5</cite> <he>אין שורין … כדי שיִשּׁוֹרוּ וכ׳</he> you must not lay in ink-materials or dyes …, unless they can be dissolved (or soaked through) before the Sabbath sets in.

senses.gloss: to be soaked, dissolved. Y. Ber. IX, 13ᵈ bot. כדי שתִּשָּׁרֶה וכ׳, v. מְגוּפָה; Y. Taan. I, 64ᵇ top שתשרף (corr. acc.).
units: Gen. R. s. 17, end אדם … מיד היא נִשְׁרֵית … אינו נִשְׁרֶה man is made out of earth, when you put a drop of water on it, it is at once dissolved (soft), but woman is made of a bone, which is not dissolved, even if you let it lie in water for many days. Y. Sabb. XIV, 14ᶜ top כל … והיא נשרית … ושאינה נשרית וכ׳ when you put salt in, and it dissolves, it is called salt water, but when it is not dissolved, it is called halmé; a. e.—
<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 1:5">Sabb. I, 5</cite> <he>יִשּׁוֹרוּ</he> (fr. <cite ref="U01054"><he>שור</he></cite> or <he>נשר</he>), v. supra.
